mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest, and an object in motion will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: An object will accelerate whenever any force, no matter how small, is applied to it.
options.C: Objects naturally tend to move in circles unless a force stops them.
options.D: A moving object will eventually stop even if no force acts on it.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest will stay at rest, and an object in motion will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Option A precisely states Newton's first law (the law of inertia). It mentions both the rest condition and uniform straight‑line motion, and the requirement of a net external force to change that state. Options B, C and D are common misconceptions: B ignores the need for net force, C confuses inertia with circular motion, and D incorrectly suggests motion ceases without a force.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate first law to balanced forces
mcqs.question: A block on a frictionless horizontal surface has a net external force of zero. According to Newton's first law, which statement must be true?

options.A: The block must be at rest.
options.B: The block must be moving with constant velocity.
options.C: The block will either remain at rest or continue moving with constant velocity.

mcqs.answer: The block will either remain at rest or continue moving with constant velocity.
mcqs.explanation: When the net external force is zero, the forces are balanced. Newton's first law then tells us the block's state of motion will not change—it can stay at rest or keep moving at the same speed in a straight line. Option C captures both possibilities. Option A is too restrictive, B ignores the rest case, and D contradicts the law.

mcqs.question: Which everyday situation best illustrates the concept of inertia?

options.A: A ball rolls down a slope and speeds up as it descends.
options.B: A passenger lurches forward when a car suddenly stops.
options.C: A kite rises higher when the wind speed increases.

mcqs.answer: A passenger lurches forward when a car suddenly stops.
mcqs.explanation: When the car stops abruptly, the passenger's body tends to continue moving forward due to its inertia, demonstrating the resistance of a body to a change in its state of motion. Option A shows acceleration due to gravity, not inertia. Option C involves wind force, and D involves magnetic attraction—neither relates to inertia.

mcqs.question: In a competitive examination, which of the following is the most precise statement of Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: A body at rest will stay at rest, and a moving body will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: A body will move faster if any force is applied to it, regardless of direction.
options.C: Objects naturally move in circles unless a force stops them.
options.D: A moving body will eventually stop even if no external force acts on it.

mcqs.answer: A body at rest will stay at rest, and a moving body will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately and concisely captures Newton's first law (law of inertia) as expected in competitive exams. Options B, C, and D are incorrect: B ignores the need for net force, C confuses inertia with circular motion, and D incorrectly states that motion ceases without a force.
